newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares rally but face downside pressure.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares rally but face downside pressure.

text.p: Singapore shares continued their rally in early Tuesday trade, but dealers said there was still sufficient downside pressure to make a long-term recovery far from plain sailing.
"It's not going to be a straight cruise back up to the 2,200 level. There's still uncertainty from the results season and on U.S. interest rates," one dealer said.
"There is some new commitment, but gains are coming more from traders selling short than anything else," another said.
At 0215 GMT, the key Straits Times Industrials Index had gained almost one percent, up 19.03 points at 2,113.43.

Monday's property stock-fuelled rally saw the sector's counters continue to gain, with City Developments leading the gainers, rising Singapore $0.40 to S$13.50, and Singapore Land up S$0.20 at S$7.70 by 0215 GMT.
In early trade gainers outstripped losers by 219 to 29, but low volume of 43 million units reflected dealers' views that bottom fishing, not broad sentiment, was driving the rise.
Early losers were topped by Great Eastern Life, down S$0.20 at S$21.00.
